reason: The source provides a context-local structured error handler, and the old harness never installs one. The packet does not establish that XInclude is enabled by the supplied build defaults. It also does not show whether passing the document node satisfies xmlXIncludeProcessNode's node->doc guard, so the frozen condition that an input exercises an XInclude error remains unresolved.

scope_contract.reason: The new setter configures the same XInclude context that the target creates and processes.

feasible_trigger.reason: An input can supply XML containing an XInclude error, and the source supports processing a document root. The recipe does not establish the XInclude build default, and the target passes the document node where xmlXIncludeProcessNode requires node->doc to be non-NULL.

evidence.dependency_reason: An invalid parse attribute produces an XInclude error when processing reaches the include.
The target's document-node argument must pass the node->doc guard.
The source's document-level route passes the document root to XInclude processing.
The recipe delegates feature defaults to configuration and attempts to build the xinclude target.

observable_consequence.reason: Without a configured handler, the context-local callback and supplied data cannot receive XInclude errors; parser and XPointer forwarding also depend on a non-NULL context handler.

evidence.dependency_reason: XInclude errors use the context handler and data.
Included-document parser forwarding is conditional on the context handler.
XPointer forwarding is conditional on the context handler.
Context creation zero-initializes the handler fields.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The complete target sequence has no setter call. Its generic variadic error function is not a context-local structured callback carrying supplied data; the delegated routes require the same unset context handler.

evidence.dependency_reason: The registered generic function has a variadic signature.
The structured setter is what assigns the context handler and data.
Parser forwarding requires a non-NULL context handler.
XPointer forwarding requires a non-NULL context handler.

identity_preserved.reason: The assessment consistently concerns delivery through a handler and data configured on the target's XInclude context. The added setter establishes that capability after the change; the old harness is fixed.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Shows XInclude error delivery through the context fields.
Shows the document-node guard affecting the proposed trigger.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Initializes only a generic error function.
Shows input control over options and entities.
Shows the delegated configuration and xinclude build attempt.

missing_information: The XInclude enablement default used by the supplied autogen.sh recipe.
Whether the document returned by xmlCtxtReadMemory has a non-NULL doc field when cast to xmlNodePtr.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: Deliver an XInclude error to a structured callback with the data configured on its XInclude context.
coverage_witness.required_setup: XInclude enabled; configure a non-NULL structured handler and data on the context, then process a document root containing an include that emits an error.
coverage_witness.actual_target_setup: The target installs a generic error function, creates a zero-initialized XInclude context, sets flags, and passes the document node to xmlXIncludeProcessNode without setting a structured handler.
coverage_witness.blocked_behavior: The context-local structured callback and its data cannot receive an error with the old setup.
coverage_witness.equivalent_routes: The generic error function and conditional parser/XPointer forwarding do not configure or deliver to that context-local callback and data.
